items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: And we became friends after that, you know.

ctx.x: Then -- and he came up to me and he says, -- I says, 'Aren't you --' He says -- I says, 'Aren't you Frankie Trumbauer?' He says, 'Yeah.' I says, 'I know it.' I says, 'I met you --' He cut me off to let me know he remembered me. I says, 'I met you --' He says, 'With Paul Whiteman,' he said, 'in Dallas.' He said, 'You had on short pants.' So you know what he said to me? I swear to God. He

says, "I see you practiced, you have practiced." He remembered he had -- I says, "You remember you told me that?" He says, "Sure, I remember." He says, "I see you practiced." He says, "You have the prettiest subtones of anybody I've ever heard in my life," I swear to God he told me that. He says, "Because you make them. When you go down to that B natural and B flat, you don't blast them." He say, "You subtoning and it sounds just like you're playing all over your horn." He says, "Keep that in." He said -- I swear…
